MethodsX 2026-12-01 Medium

EchoGO: annotation-context-aware functional interpretation of transcriptomic data.

EchoGO is a reproducible framework for functional enrichment of transcriptomic data that uses GOseq as the primary evidence while comparing results across multiple organism annotation contexts with experiment-specific backgrounds. It assembles evidence at the GO-term level with analytical and organism provenance, helping address incomplete annotation and uneven identifier recognition.

Cell reports methods 2026-11-12 High

PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.

PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (up to 100 million), and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large-scale transcriptomic atlases.

Nucleic acids research 2026-11-10 Medium

gcPathogen 2.0: an expanded multi-omics database advancing global pathogen surveillance and One Health research.

gcPathogen 2.0 is a major update to a pathogen genomic surveillance database, expanding coverage from 1,134 to 1,506 pathogenic species and surpassing 2.3 million genomic records. The update adds integrated genomic and transcriptional profiles, systematic tracking of cross-habitat distribution, and large-scale antimicrobial peptide discovery, supporting One Health research across bacteria, fungi, viruses, and parasites.

Nucleic acids research 2026-11-05 Medium

Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC): an integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform.

Met-SC is a new integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform that supports standardized deposition of metabolomics data across LC-MS, CE-MS, and NMR workflows, along with spectral resource management and online analysis tools. It contains over 7.7 million reference spectra and adds disease-focused knowledge mining, aiming to make metabolomics data easier to store, analyze, and reuse.

JMIR AI 2026-11-03 Medium

Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.

ChatDRex is a conversational multi-agent platform that integrates disease module identification and drug repurposing prediction by coordinating specialized agents over heterogeneous biomedical data and networks. It aims to lower the barrier to complex in silico repurposing workflows by letting users interact in natural language while agents handle data integration and analysis. The work is a platform-development study, so its main contribution is the architecture and workflow rather than a validated new repurposing candidate.

Nucleic acids research 2026-11-02 High

InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.

InterPro is a freely accessible database that integrates predictive models from multiple member databases to classify protein sequences into families and identify domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, covering UniProtKB extensively and linking to resources like Gene Ontology and PDBe. This makes it a central hub for protein functional annotation.

Toxicology 2026-11-01 Low

Crystalline silica particles exposure modulated miRNA expression profiles in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells.

This study profiled miRNA expression changes in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells after exposure to crystalline silica particles, identifying both intracellular and extracellular (secreted) miRNA responses. The findings suggest that specific miRNAs could serve as effect biomarkers of silica exposure in human biomonitoring. The work is preliminary and limited to a single cell line, but provides a starting point for developing exposure biomarkers for silicosis and related diseases.

Development of a Knowledge Map for Managing Symptoms of Graft-Versus-Host Disease in Patients Undergoing Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.

This review synthesizes evidence on managing graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) symptoms after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation to build a structured knowledge graph for nursing interventions. The goal is to give nurses a systematic tool for addressing GVHD symptoms across multiple organ systems, where current practice lacks structured guidance.

The Journal of investigative dermatology 2026-11-01 Medium

Cutibacterium acnes induces T-cell extracellular traps with distinct proteome programs.

This study shows that both acne-associated and healthy skin-associated strains of Cutibacterium acnes rapidly trigger extracellular trap release from human neutrophils and Th17 T cells. While neutrophil extracellular traps had a conserved proteomic profile regardless of strain, T-cell extracellular traps (TETs) exhibited distinct proteome programs depending on the C. acnes strain, suggesting strain-specific functional consequences in acne pathogenesis.

CPT: pharmacometrics & systems pharmacology 2026-11-01 Medium

Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer.

This perspective argues that AI-driven multi-modal data analysis should be reconceived not as a tool for integrating data into quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models, but as a new layer that generates quantitative measurements. In this reframing, QSP serves as a conceptual foundational model of biology while AI supplies the quantitative inputs, potentially reshaping how mechanistic drug-development models are built and parameterized.

Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society 2026-11-01 Medium

PDBe-SIFTS: An open-source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search.

PDBe-SIFTS is a new open-source, locally deployable tool that maps UniProt protein sequences to PDB structures at residue-level resolution. It improves on the original SIFTS pipeline by using MMseqs2 for fast sequence search, a better scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and connectivity-based refinement of residue alignments. This makes high-quality structure-function mapping accessible to any lab without relying on internal PDBe infrastructure.

The Journal of biological chemistry 2026-11-01 Medium

EXPERT: A practical and forward-looking guide to capturing protein expression and purification metadata to develop machine learning models.

The paper introduces EXPERT, a structured reporting template for capturing protein expression and purification metadata in a consistent, standardized way. The authors argue that inconsistent experimental reporting is a major barrier to building effective machine learning models for protein engineering and bioprocess optimization, and propose the essential data fields that should be recorded during expression and purification workflows.

Single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas decodes bone development, diseases, and regeneration.

This review synthesizes how single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling, especially scATAC-seq, has been applied to map the epigenetic regulatory landscape of bone development, skeletal disease, and regeneration. It highlights how these technologies reveal transcription factor binding programs and gene regulatory networks that control bone cell fate at single-cell resolution, and discusses how these maps can inform understanding of skeletal pathologies and regenerative strategies.

JMIR medical informatics 2026-10-29 Medium

A Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph for Hypertension With Emotional Comorbidity: Development and Blinded Question-Answering Evaluation.

This paper develops a focused knowledge graph that organizes traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension with emotional comorbidities such as anxiety, depression, and insomnia, linking syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs to their sources. It then evaluates the knowledge graph's contribution to generated answers through a blinded question-answering assessment. The work demonstrates how a domain-specific knowledge graph can support grounded, source-traceable answers in a specialized clinical domain.

Poultry science 2026-10-28 Medium

Integration of genotyping by sequencing and machine learning for genome-wide identification of informative markers for body weight in broiler chickens.

This study combined cost-effective genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) with two ensemble machine learning methods, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Machine, to identify SNP markers associated with body weight at hatch and 3 weeks in broiler chickens. The approach demonstrates that GBS plus ML can serve as a cheaper alternative to high-density SNP arrays for genome-wide association studies in poultry breeding. The work highlights informative markers that could support marker-assisted selection for growth traits.

Plant biotechnology journal 2026-10-28 Medium

Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.

This paper describes how the CABBI research center used a Design-Build-Test-Learn framework to coordinate efforts across molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment to engineer C4 grasses (such as sugarcane and sorghum) to accumulate oil (triacylglycerol) in their vegetative tissues rather than just seeds. It reports lessons from this vertically integrated, multi-disciplinary approach to producing renewable fuels and biobased chemicals from high-biomass crops.

bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 2026-10-27 Medium

Phenologs at knowledge-graph scale: a mouse-to-slime-mold catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases.

The authors compute phenologs—statistically significant overlaps between human disease genes and model-organism phenotype genes linked by orthology—at knowledge-graph scale using the Monarch Knowledge Graph, covering human and seven model species. Using PANTHER protein families as an orthology framework, they produce a catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases, including cross-species links such as mouse-to-slime-mold. This provides a systematic, principled resource for transferring model-organism gene-phenotype knowledge to human disease gene discovery.

OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.

OmniVira is a curated knowledgebase that consolidates literature-derived evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission into structured, source-linked records. It uses an auditable framework that connects individual findings and supporting text to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, making dispersed surveillance, epidemiological, and genomic evidence reusable and traceable.

Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.

This retrospective multicenter study develops a biomarker-aware Transformer model that leverages longitudinal electronic health record data to predict the onset of acute kidney injury and to forecast patient prognosis after onset. The approach addresses the high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity of EHR data, aiming to support earlier prevention and better post-onset care decisions.

JMIR mental health 2026-10-23 Medium

Meta Mesh Ontology for Cross-Domain Mental Health Knowledge Integration: Development and Evaluation Study.

This paper develops and evaluates a Meta Mesh Ontology designed to integrate mental health knowledge across different domains, addressing the limitations of rigid categorical diagnostic systems like DSM-5 and ICD-11. The ontology aims to capture the complexity, heterogeneity, and dynamic nature of mental disorders, including multifactorial etiologies, dimensional symptom profiles, and comorbidity. It represents an effort to provide a more flexible knowledge representation framework for psychiatric classification.

scSpatial: an atlas for single-cell spatial omics.

scSpatial is a new atlas/database that aggregates single-cell spatial omics datasets, which were previously scattered across individual publications. It integrates spatial coordinates with molecular profiles and cell identities to support construction of spatially resolved cell atlases and characterization of disease-associated tissue remodeling. The resource aims to make SCSO data more accessible and reusable for the community.

Frontiers in neuroergonomics 2026-01-01 Low

Closed-loop cognitive state control: a hypothesis framework for real-time estimation, stabilization, and recovery of task-specific high-performance cognitive states.

This hypothesis paper proposes a framework for 'closed-loop cognitive state control,' in which an individual's task-specific high-performance cognitive states are rapidly entered, stabilized, and recovered using real-time multimodal sensing. Cognition is modeled as a partially observable dynamical system whose latent states are inferred from behavioral, physiological, and contextual signals. The work is conceptual and does not present empirical validation.

Frontiers in oncology 2026-01-01 Medium

Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.

This review argues that computationally predicted metabolic vulnerabilities in cancer are not equivalent to experimentally confirmed ones, and that the field often conflates the two. It surveys how AI and genome-scale systems biology generate metabolic hypotheses at scale, and calls for clearer evidentiary standards before predictions are treated as validated synthetic lethal targets.

Artificial Intelligence as a Multifaceted Toolkit for Antibacterial Drug Discovery against Resistance.

This review argues that AI can be applied as a structured toolkit across antibacterial drug discovery and development to combat antimicrobial resistance, rather than as a single isolated technique. It emphasizes AI's strengths in integrating multi-omics data and recognizing complex patterns to address slow antibiotic discovery, limited target diversity, and single-mechanism drug design. The paper frames AI applications across different resistance mechanisms and translational stages.

Sustainable nutrition: integrating food systems, environmental science, and diet to advance public and planetary health.

This perspective proposes 'sustainable nutrition' as a unifying concept that links dietary intake and health outcomes with food production, processing, access, consumption, and environmental sustainability. It argues that advancing public and planetary health requires understanding nutrition within these broader food-system and environmental contexts rather than focusing on intake and metabolism alone.
